study: Reinke, Herman & Dong (2018), Incredible Years Teacher Classroom Management (IY TCM), group RCT, Prevention Science
eval_evidence: Evaluation conducted and authored by the IES-funded research team (Reinke & Herman, Univ. of Missouri; IES R305A100342) that also implemented/delivered the IY TCM trial. While the IY TCM curriculum itself was created by Webster-Stratton (third party), the impact study was run and authored by the team delivering the program, with no independent third-party evaluator.
developer_evidence: PD was delivered directly by the research team's certified personnel: trainings 'were cofacilitated by two doctoral-level IY TCM group leaders' and coaching by a certified IY TCM group facilitator. The study team (not trained school intermediaries) delivered the workshops and coaching.
cascade_evidence: Research-team-certified IY TCM group leaders trained the teachers directly in the monthly workshops and coached them directly; no train-the-trainer/lead-teacher intermediary hop.
counterfactual_evidence: Control teachers placed on a 'wait list, business as usual control group' (offered IY TCM two years later); no alternative treatment. All 9 schools already implemented SW-PBIS, so both arms shared that backdrop, but the control got no alternative PD.
coaching_evidence: IY TCM embeds in-class coaching in its model: 'After and between each training session, teachers are followed by a coach', across the ~6 monthly workshops (Oct-Feb). Recurring in-classroom coaching cycles by a certified coach.
student_dose_evidence: Intervention targets teachers' classroom-management practice only; no direct student-facing tutoring, pull-out, added minutes, or software dose.
maturity_evidence: Outcomes measured at the end of the single intervention school year (pre ~October, post ~April/May of the same year); teachers were new to IY TCM that year (control on a 2-year wait list). First implementation year.
